q.t: A fair coin is tossed. What is the probability of getting a head?
q.e: There are 2 equally likely outcomes (head, tail) and 1 of them is a head: 1 out of 2.

q.t: A fair die is thrown. What is the probability of getting a 4?
q.e: 6 equally likely faces, and only one of them is 4.

q.t: How many possible outcomes are there when a die is thrown once?
q.e: The faces 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6.

q.t: What is the probability of an event that is certain to happen?
q.e: All of the outcomes are favourable, so favourable ÷ total = 1.

q.t: What is the probability of an impossible event?
q.e: None of the outcomes is favourable: 0 ÷ total = 0.

q.t: A die is thrown. What is the probability of getting a 7?
q.e: A die has no face with 7, so it can never happen.

q.t: A bag has 3 red and 2 blue balls. One ball is drawn without looking. What is the probability that it is red?
q.e: 3 red balls out of 5 balls in all.

q.t: How many possible outcomes are there when a coin is tossed once?
q.e: Head or tail.

q.t: The probability of any event always lies:
q.e: Favourable outcomes can be none (0) or at most all of them (1) — never more than the total.

q.t: A die is thrown. What is the probability of getting an even number?
q.e: Even faces: 2, 4, 6 — that is 3 out of 6 = 1/2.

q.t: A die is thrown. What is the probability of getting a prime number?
q.e: Primes on a die: 2, 3 and 5 (1 is not prime). 3 out of 6 = 1/2.

q.t: A die is thrown. What is the probability of getting a number greater than 4?
q.e: Greater than 4 means 5 or 6: 2 out of 6 = 1/3.

q.t: A bag has 5 red, 3 green and 2 blue balls. What is the probability of drawing a green ball?
q.e: 3 green out of 5 + 3 + 2 = 10 balls.

q.t: A bag has 5 red, 3 green and 2 blue balls. What is the probability of drawing a ball that is NOT red?
q.e: Not red = green or blue = 5 balls out of 10 = 1/2. (Also 1 − 5/10.)

q.t: Cards numbered 1 to 20 are shuffled and one is drawn. What is the probability that it is a multiple of 5?
q.e: Multiples of 5: 5, 10, 15, 20 — four cards. 4/20 = 1/5.

q.t: A coin is tossed 100 times and lands heads 46 times. What is the experimental probability of a tail?
q.e: Tails = 100 − 46 = 54. Experimental probability = 54/100 = 27/50, based on what actually happened.

q.t: A letter is chosen at random from the word MATHEMATICS. What is the probability that it is M?
q.e: The word has 11 letters and M appears twice.

q.t: For any event E, P(E) + P(not E) equals:
q.e: Every outcome is either in E or not in E, so together they cover all the outcomes.

q.t: A spinner has 8 equal sectors numbered 1 to 8. What is the probability that it stops on an odd number?
A day of the week is chosen at random. What is the probability that its name begins with T?
q.e: Tuesday and Thursday — 2 out of 7 days.

q.t: Cards numbered 1 to 25 are shuffled and one is drawn. What is the probability that it is a prime number?
q.k: F(len([n for n in range(2,26) if all(n%d for d in range(2,n))]),25)
q.e: Primes up to 25: 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17, 19, 23 — nine of them.

q.t: Cards numbered 1 to 25 are shuffled and one is drawn. What is the probability that it is a perfect square?
q.e: Squares: 1, 4, 9, 16, 25 — five cards. 5/25 = 1/5.

q.t: A letter is chosen at random from the word EQUATION. What is the probability that it is a vowel?
q.e: 8 letters; the vowels are E, U, A, I, O — five of them.

q.t: A die is thrown 200 times. The faces 1 to 6 come up 30, 35, 28, 40, 32 and 35 times. What is the experimental probability of a 4?
q.e: 4 came up 40 times out of 200: 40/200 = 1/5 — close to, but not exactly, the theoretical 1/6.

q.t: A die is thrown 200 times. The faces 1 to 6 come up 30, 35, 28, 40, 32 and 35 times. What is the experimental probability of an even number?
The probability of an event is 0.35. What is the probability that it does NOT happen?
q.e: The two probabilities add to 1: 1 − 0.35 = 0.65.

q.t: A bag has 6 red balls and some blue balls. The probability of drawing a red ball is 2/5. How many blue balls are there?
q.e: 6 is 2/5 of the total, so the total is 15. Blue = 15 − 6 = 9.

q.t: A number is chosen at random from 1 to 30. What is the probability that it is divisible by 3 or by 5?
q.k: F(len([n for n in range(1,31) if n%3==0 or n%5==0]),30)
q.e: Multiples of 3: 10. Multiples of 5: 6. But 15 and 30 were counted twice, so 10 + 6 − 2 = 14. 14/30 = 7/15.

q.t: Which of these CANNOT be the probability of an event?
q.e: A probability is favourable ÷ total, which can never be more than 1.

q.t: A class has 40 students, of whom 25 are girls. One student is chosen at random. What is the probability of choosing a boy?
Two coins are tossed together. What is the probability of getting exactly one head?
q.e: The 4 equally likely outcomes are HH, HT, TH, TT. Exactly one head: HT and TH — 2 out of 4. (HT and TH are different outcomes.)

q.t: Two coins are tossed together. What is the probability of getting at least one head?
q.e: HH, HT and TH all have a head — 3 out of 4. Quicker: 1 − P(no head) = 1 − 1/4.

q.t: Two dice are thrown together. What is the probability that the numbers add up to 7?
q.k: F(len([1 for a in range(1,7) for b in range(1,7) if a+b==7]),36)

q.t: Two dice are thrown together. What is the probability of getting the same number on both?
q.e: The doubles are (1,1), (2,2) … (6,6) — six of the 36 outcomes.

q.t: A bag has red and blue balls in the ratio 3 : 5. What is the probability of drawing a blue ball?
q.e: Out of every 8 balls, 5 are blue.

q.t: A box has 100 bulbs, 8 of them defective. One GOOD bulb is taken out and kept aside. What is the probability that the next bulb drawn is defective?
q.e: Now 99 bulbs remain, and all 8 defective ones are still among them.

q.t: Cards numbered 1 to 50 are shuffled and one is drawn. What is the probability that it is NOT a multiple of 7?
q.e: Multiples of 7 up to 50: 7, 14, 21, 28, 35, 42, 49 — seven cards. So 50 − 7 = 43 are not.

q.t: A game can only be won or lost. P(win) = 3x and P(lose) = 2x. Find P(win).
q.e: The two probabilities add to 1: 5x = 1, so x = 1/5 and P(win) = 3/5.

q.t: A letter is chosen at random from the word PROBABILITY. What is the probability that it is B or I?
q.e: 11 letters. B appears twice and I appears twice: 4 favourable letters.

q.t: Three coins are tossed together. What is the probability that all three show the same face?
q.e: There are 2 × 2 × 2 = 8 outcomes. All the same: HHH or TTT — 2 out of 8 = 1/4.
